StackType.rationale: PowerStackType.Counter. The sim has no StackType concept; Power.on_stack (powers.py:64-66) adds unconditionally, which is what PowerCmd.ModifyAmount does (PowerCmd.cs:236 -- no StackType branch). Third-file citations, not hashed here.

AfterDeath.issue: RE-VERDICTED 2026-07-26 (review fix pass): `deliberate-divergence` -> `gap`. The old rationale was that this unit "repairs the only observable it produces" by restoring `hp = max_hp = 999_999_999` from on_damage_received (powers.py:2022-2033), mirroring WaterfallGiant.cs:305's `CreatureCmd.SetMaxAndCurrentHp(base.Creature, 999999999m)`. **That is false on three counts.** (a) It repairs the HP DISPLAY only. It does not restore the AfterDeath dispatch, so every non-owner listener the game pays out to is still missed -- see the Gremlin Horn witness on power/adaptable's AfterDeath entry, which applies verbatim here (the Waterfall Giant is the ported Underdocks boss, rooms.py:139 and monsters/underdocks/waterfall_giant.py:148-151, and Gremlin Horn is a ported Uncommon relic whose AfterDeath carries no wasRemovalPrevented guard, GremlinHorn.cs:24-32). Feed applies too: SteamEruptionPower does not override ShouldOwnerDeathTriggerFatal (default true, PowerModel.cs:646-649) and Feed.cs:42 gates on DamageResult.WasTargetKilled, which DamageResult.cs:89-99 documents as true even when the death is prevented, so the game grants +3 max HP for Feeding the giant to death and cards/feed.py:45's `if target.is_dead` grants nothing. `InvokeDiedEvent` (CreatureCmd.cs:507) likewise has no counterpart. (b) The repair runs from a dispatch the game deliberately SKIPS on a killing blow -- CreatureCmd.cs:392's `if (!WasTargetKilled || !originalTarget.IsDead)`, which the sim mirrors at cmds.py:115-122 -- and it only fires in the sim because the prevention branch reset hp to 1 first, making `target.is_dead` False. So the repair is BUILT ON damage_pipeline gap G4 rather than being independent of it. (c) It does not fire at all on the non-damage kill path (cmds.py:191-205, which has no on_damage_received call), leaving the giant at hp 1 instead of 999999999; see this record's non-damage-kill guard. LIVE via (a): the Gremlin Horn payout and the Feed payout are both reachable in an ordinary Waterfall Giant fight. ONE MECHANISM, ONE VERDICT (binding rule 3): power/adaptable, power/illusion and power/steam_eruption all implement a C# AfterDeath body by returning False from `should_die` (powers.py:3365-3369, :1566-1570, :2016-2020), so all three run the sim's single death-PREVENTION branch (cmds.py:106-113) where C# runs the REAL-DEATH branch (CreatureCmd.cs:505-559). None of the three overrides ShouldDie, and all three bodies sit behind `!wasRemovalPrevented` (AdaptablePower.cs:34, IllusionPower.cs:79, SteamEruptionPower.cs:17) -- i.e. they are explicitly EXCLUDED from the branch the sim is executing. All three therefore carry `gap`; steam_eruption's `deliberate-divergence` was corrected to `gap` in the 2026-07-26 review fix pass. The canonical statement of the shared observable (the Gremlin Horn witness) is on power/adaptable's AfterDeath entry.

ShouldStopCombatFromEnding.issue: No sim counterpart. C# reads this through Hook.ShouldStopCombatFromEnding at CombatManager.cs:196, inside the win check: while any power returns true the combat cannot end. `hooks.py` defines no such hook and combat.py:272-277 decides the win purely from `is_gone` over the non-minion enemies. The sim reaches the same OUTCOME here by the mid-death spawn / death prevention described on this record's death entry, which keeps `_all_enemies_dead()` false on its own, so DORMANT -- but the mechanism is absent, and a future power wanting to hold combat open without also adding a creature or preventing a death would have nothing to hook. Third-file citations, not hashed here. ENGINE-LEVEL HOME (added 2026-07-26): this mechanism now also carries `gap` at audit/records/seam/creature_card_cmds.json step 8c, which owns the missing hook surface itself; same verdict at every site per rule 3.

ShouldCreatureBeRemovedFromCombatAfterDe.maps_to: hooks.py:603 -- NOT implemented by this power
ShouldCreatureBeRemovedFromCombatAfterDe.issue: The sim has the hook and this power does not use it, because it prevents the death instead. Same unused-hook finding as adaptable's and illusion's, and the same inconsistency with reattach, which does use it. ShouldPowerBeRemovedAfterOwnerDeath.rationale: `=> false`. C# strips a dead creature's powers at CreatureCmd.cs:533; the sim never removes powers on death at all, so `false` is its universal behaviour and this override is satisfied for free. The inverse -- that the C# DEFAULT is `true` and the sim strips nothing -- is an engine-wide absence reported in content-power-report-b.md rather than verdicted here. ENGINE-LEVEL SIBLING (added 2026-07-26): the INVERSE finding -- that C#'s DEFAULT is `true` so every power WITHOUT this override should be stripped on its owner's death and in the sim none is -- now carries a verdict of its own at audit/records/seam/creature_card_cmds.json step 8b (`gap`, LIVE, executed on the Decimillipede). It used to exist only as prose in content-power-report-b.md section 3c. This entry stays `faithful` because the override asks for exactly the behaviour the sim gives for free; the engine-wide absence is step 8b's, not this unit's.

The sim needs this because its restore runs from a generic damage hook rather than from the death path; without it every later hit would re-inflate the HP. Correct and load-bearing.

Closed game-wide, re-verified 2026-07-26. EXECUTED: `py audit/tools/power_census.py visible` reports 0 IsVisibleInternal overrides of 260 files. That 260 is the .cs files DIRECTLY under src/Core/Models/Powers and EXCLUDES the 16 in Powers/Mocks/ (276 including them); a recursive `grep -rn IsVisibleInternal src/Core/Models/Powers/`, which does cover Mocks/, also returns 0 -- so IsVisible is provably always true for every power in the decompiled game, mocks included. guards.what: The prevention branch's HP contract: sim `hp = 1` vs C# leaving the creature at 0 and re-entering KillWithoutCheckingWinCondition
guards.issue: Part of the should_die-for-AfterDeath mechanism, carried as its own entry because it survives any fix that only re-slots the AfterDeath body. cmds.py:112 writes `target.hp = 1` and stops. C# does NOT heal the creature: CreatureCmd.cs:560-571 leaves it at 0 HP, fires Hook.AfterDeath(wasRemovalPrevented: true) and Hook.AfterPreventingDeath, and then, `if (creature.IsDead)`, RE-ENTERS `KillWithoutCheckingWinCondition(creature, force, recursion + 1)` -- up to 10 times before throwing InvalidOperationException (:562-565). So in the game a preventer must actually raise the creature's HP (Fairy in a Bottle heals; these three do not, which is why they take C#'s DEATH branch and not this one), whereas the sim's single silent `hp = 1` makes any prevention permanent and models neither the re-entry nor the 10-deep bail-out. Two consequences beyond the 1-vs-0 HP that conformance asserts on directly: the sim cannot express a prevention that fails, and the sim's own steam_eruption HP restore only runs because this floor makes `target.is_dead` False at cmds.py:121 (damage_pipeline gap G4). Same verdict at all three sites per rule 3.

guards.what: The non-damage kill path: CreatureCmd.kill reproduces both arms but fires no on_damage_received
guards.issue: Part of the same mechanism, at the second of the sim's two death sites. `CreatureCmd.kill` (cmds.py:191-205) mirrors DamageCmd.deal's should_die / should_remove_from_combat_after_death / on_death fork and the same `target.hp = 1` prevention floor, but it is not a damage event, so it fires neither on_damage_received nor after_preventing_death. Consequences: (a) power/steam_eruption's HP restore (powers.py:2022-2033) lives on on_damage_received and therefore does not run here at all, leaving the Waterfall Giant at hp 1 instead of the 999999999 WaterfallGiant.cs:305 sets; (b) the preventer never learns the death was prevented. DORMANT for these three powers today -- the only ported non-damage kill of a steam_eruption owner is the giant's own `_explode` (monsters/underdocks/waterfall_giant.py:142-145), which runs AFTER `_about_to_blow` removed the power at :140, and nothing kills the Test Subject or an Illusion off the damage path. Named trigger: any ported non-damage kill reaching a creature that still holds one of these three powers -- SandpitPower._expire (powers.py:2610-2619) and TheGambitPower (powers.py:3816-3829) are the two ported callers of CreatureCmd.kill outside a monster's own move. Same verdict at all three sites per rule 3.
